stories.title: Config overlay persistence + layered read (config.json default <- Pi-local overlay override)
acceptance: [ATLAS DESIGN-GATE -- load-bearing config/SSOT seam] introduce a Pi-local OVERLAY file (gitignored, added to deploy-pi.sh rsync excludes like .env so deploy never clobbers it) that layers OVER config.json: effective = overlay-override ELSE config.json default. config.json stays read-only shipped default; nothing writes config.json at runtime

[GAP 2 -- A-4 SSOT, Atlas] the overlay merge is ONE shared utility in src/common/config/ (e.g. resolveEffectiveConfig(base, overlay, allowlist)) that BOTH config readers call -- the orchestrator loadConfigWithSecrets AND states_http_server._loadDisplaySection (which reads config.json directly). Effective config MUST be identical for every consumer (avoids the A-4 divergence). Allow-list enforced at BOTH read (overlay keys outside the allow-list ignored + logged) AND write (US-531 endpoint) = defense-in-depth

[GAP 3a -- one key one truth, Atlas] do NOT mint a new pi.display.carousel.autoRotate bool. The overlay stores the EXISTING pi.display.carousel.autoRotateS (seconds; 0=off, >0=on). The UI toggle derives on/off from autoRotateS>0 (off writes 0, on writes the shipped interval)

overridable-key allow-list (Slice 1): pi.display.carousel.autoRotateS, pi.power.mode, pi.alerts.audioAlerts, pi.calibration.mode, pi.analysis.triggerAfterDrive. pi.power.mode overlay value MUST validate to {car,wall,unknown} -- invalid -> unknown (honest-unknown contract), never a confident wrong mode
honest-instrument: malformed/absent overlay -> config.json default, never a guessed value; out-of-allow-list key ignored + logged

test proves: overlay override wins over default via the SHARED resolver for BOTH read paths; absent overlay -> default; out-of-allow-list key rejected; autoRotateS 0<->interval round-trips; deploy-exclude keeps the overlay across an rsync; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: set an overlay override autoRotateS=0 on the Pi, run a deploy, then read the effective value via BOTH the orchestrator and the state server
validationCriteria.outcome: both readers return 0 after the deploy (overlay preserved + wins for every consumer -- no divergence)

conditionalOutcomes: Atlas ruled the overlay contract sound 2026-08-03 (3 gaps folded). resolveEffectiveConfig is the single seam; do not merge the overlay per-reader.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want my Pi settings to survive deploys, so a toggle I set on the Pi is not wiped the next time code ships.

filesActuallyTouched: src/common/config/overlay.py (NEW -- flat dot-path overlay, Slice-1 allow-list, resolveEffectiveConfig/applyConfigOverlay/validateOverlayValue/loadOverlay/overlayPathFor)
src/common/config/secrets_loader.py (loadConfigWithSecrets resolves through the shared seam after resolveSecrets)
src/pi/splash/states_http_server.py (_loadDisplaySection resolves through the SAME seam)
deploy/deploy-pi.sh (rsync exclude + tar-fallback exclude + tar-fallback wipe PRESERVE)

stories.completionNotes:
OVERLAY CONTRACT AS BUILT: flat dot-path map (config.local.json) beside config.json; effective = allow-listed overlay override ELSE config.json default. Flat keys were the deliberate choice -- they make the allow-list a LITERAL key comparison, so US-531's write gate can reuse validateOverlayValue() unchanged instead of writing a second recursive walk that would drift from this one. US-531: import validateOverlayValue + overlayPathFor from common.config.overlay; do NOT re-implement the allow-list.

GAP 2 (A-4 SSOT) SATISFIED AND MUTATION-PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED. Both readers call applyConfigOverlay. The load-bearing test is test_bothReadPaths_agreeOnEffectiveAutoRotateS -- parametrized [0, 8, 20] because 8 equals the shipped default and would stay GREEN under a broken reader. Mutation A (drop the seam from _loadDisplaySection) -> 3 red, and test_loadConfigWithSecrets_appliesOverlay STAYED GREEN: a per-reader test suite would ship the exact A-4 divergence this story exists to prevent. Mutation B (drop it from loadConfigWithSecrets) -> 4 red. Both reverted by hand (git checkout is outside the allow-list) and re-verified green.

HONEST BOUND ON test_bothReadPaths_agreeOnRejectingAnOutOfAllowListKey: it cannot detect a missing seam, because a rejected key leaves BOTH readers on the default either way. It pins the rejection, not the wiring. The autoRotateS parity test is the one that pins the wiring -- do not delete it as redundant.

GAP 3a HONOURED: no pi.display.carousel.autoRotate bool was minted. autoRotateS (0=off, >0=on) is the only key; US-532's toggle derives on/off from >0 and writes 0 / the shipped interval.

HONEST-INSTRUMENT, MECHANISM-PINNED: invalid pi.power.mode coerces to 'unknown' (NOT to the config.json default -- a corrupt mode means the deployment context is unknown, and base could legitimately ship 'car'). Mutation C (fall back to default instead of coercing) -> 6 red; note the WARNING log still said 'resolving to unknown' while the code no longer did, i.e. the log is a DECLARATION and only the assertion pins the MECHANISM. Out-of-allow-list keys are ignored + logged and never invent a config branch (proven against the REAL config.json: a planted pi.obd.port override raised KeyError('obd') = nothing created). Wrong-typed values fall back to the default; bool is explicitly excluded from the numeric check so True cannot pass as autoRotateS.

DEPLOY DURABILITY -- THE TAR FALLBACK HAD A SECOND HOLE. deploy-pi.sh has TWO sync paths. Excluding config.local.json from the tarball is NOT sufficient: the fallback wipes the remote top level BEFORE extracting, so the overlay also needed a `! -name` entry in the preserve find. Excluding from the tarball alone would have silently deleted the operator's settings on any deploy from a machine without rsync. All three edits landed + tested separately.

REAL-CONFIG SMOKE (dev box, beyond the synthetic fixtures): planted an overlay next to the SHIPPED config.json -> both readers returned autoRotateS=0, power.mode=wall, pi.obd.port rejected+logged ONCE PER READER (both gates fire). `git status --ignored` confirmed `!!` on config.local.json -- git ACTUALLY ignores it, not merely a .gitignore line. Artifacts removed; tree clean.

STILL OWED BY THE VALIDATION CRITERIA -- DO NOT READ GREEN AS DONE: the AC's 'overlay survives an rsync' is asserted against deploy-pi.sh TEXT, not a real rsync. The real proof is the PM's Pi deploy: set autoRotateS=0 in /home/mcornelison/Projects/Eclipse-01/config.local.json, deploy, confirm the file still exists and BOTH readers return 0. Also note a carousel-config change needs an eclipse-states-http bounce (injected + cached at startup -- US-533 GAP 1 / US-536 deploy note).

BLAST RADIUS: loadConfigWithSecrets is the project-wide config entry point, so this is a base-module change -- PM should run the FULL suite at integration. In-loop I ran the story file (42) + the consumer suites of both touched readers: 360 passed, 1 skipped (test_token.py:70 POSIX file-mode gate on Windows -- PRE-EXISTING, documented by US-525, not mine). ruff clean on all 4 .py files; `bash -n deploy/deploy-pi.sh` clean (pytest cannot see a shell syntax error); validate_config.py passes through the new seam. Behaviour is a strict no-op when no overlay file exists, which is the shipped state.

TD-075 still stands: `ruff check src/ tests/` exits 1 on a clean tree (10 project-wide errors in src/calibration/speed_aligner-spool.py + tests/pm/*), so lint was per-touched-file. `make` is NOT on PATH here -- `make lint` exits 127, which READS LIKE A PASS.

FOR PM: a new inbox item appeared during this iteration whose filename names US-536's subject (Atlas RCA on --disable-gpu crashing the renderer). Not my lane to read -- flagging only because disposition-B (US-536) REVERTS --disable-gpu and this may bear on it. Read it before dispatching US-536.

stories.title: Token-gated settings write endpoint on states_http_server (writes the overlay)
acceptance: [ATLAS SEAM -- CONFIRMED] add a THIRD token-gated POST route on states_http_server following the existing US-403/US-407 pattern exactly (if not self._tokenOk(): 401). The kiosk is chromium JS + cannot write files, so a toggle POSTs here to write the US-530 overlay
[SECURITY -- Atlas US-525 ruling] token-gated with the US-393 SSOT token; NEVER weaken/bypass _tokenOk, no un-authenticated write surface (= TD-067 / Atlas BLOCK)
validates the key against the US-530 allow-list + the value type (numeric for autoRotateS; bool for the 3 toggles; {car,wall,unknown} for pi.power.mode); out-of-allow-list/invalid -> 4xx, NO write
atomic overlay write (temp + rename); honest response -- return the REAL stored effective value, never optimistic success
test proves: authenticated allow-listed write persists to the overlay; un-authenticated write rejected; out-of-allow-list/invalid rejected with no write; ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: POST an allow-listed setting change with the token, then without the token
validationCriteria.outcome: with token -> overlay updated + real effective value returned; without token -> 401 + overlay unchanged

stories.goal: As the operator, I want the settings screen to save my toggles, so tapping a toggle persists it -- without opening any un-gated write surface on the Pi.

renders the 5 Slice-1 settings with their CURRENT EFFECTIVE values (read via the US-530 shared resolver, surfaced through the state server): auto-rotate (derived from autoRotateS>0), power mode (car/wall/unknown), audio alerts, calibration mode, auto-analyze after drive

honest save flow (per Iris): each control writes via the US-531 token-gated endpoint; on write failure the control reflects the REAL stored value, never an optimistic success; where a change needs a service restart to apply it is labeled plainly (NOT a silent no-op)
matches the F-124 carousel design system (tokens, Oswald wordmark); test/probe proves the band renders the 5 controls with effective values inside the setup-menu overlay; ruff/lint clean

validationCriteria.outcome: the band shows the 5 controls with real effective values, matching Iris's Option-B design + the honest save flow

stories.title: Wire the 5 config settings end-to-end (read effective + write overlay + apply semantics)
acceptance: wire each of the 5 controls: reads its effective value (US-530 shared resolver), writes via the token-gated endpoint (US-531), and applies per its consumer

[GAP 1 -- Atlas: 'applies LIVE' is FALSE for auto-rotate] states_http_server reads pi.display.carousel ONCE at startup and injects it cached (window.DISPLAY_CAROUSEL). Changing autoRotateS needs an eclipse-states-http BOUNCE + page reload -- NOT a dashboard/chromium restart. So the auto-rotate toggle: the write endpoint bounces eclipse-states-http + triggers a reload, and the UI honestly labels 'applies on restart'. Do NOT claim live

pi.power.mode -> PowerModeProvider re-emits mode on its next cycle (fixes bench unknown -> wall); pi.alerts.audioAlerts / pi.calibration.mode / pi.analysis.triggerAfterDrive -> apply live if the consumer re-reads, else the band states 'takes effect on next boot/restart'
honest-instrument: no control silently no-ops; pi.power.mode is a 3-state selector (car|wall|unknown), unknown remains the honest default
test proves each of the 5 settings round-trips (render effective -> change -> overlay written -> effective value/behavior reflects it, or the honest restart-label shows); ruff clean

validationCriteria.action: set auto-rotate on in the band (states-http bounces), then set power mode to wall
validationCriteria.outcome: auto-rotate resumes after the states-http bounce (labeled honestly, not claimed live); power tile reads WALL; both survive a reboot via the overlay

stories.goal: As the operator, I want each Settings control to actually change behavior, so toggling it takes real effect (or honestly tells me when it will).

stories.title: Freeze disposition-B: revert US-522 --disable-gpu + land autoRotateS:0 default
acceptance: [CIO disposition-B 2026-08-03, via Atlas] REVERT US-522's --disable-gpu from the eclipse-dashboard kiosk ExecStart (both dashboard.service.x11 + .wayland) -- keep the GPU ON. KEEP --password-store=basic (keyring fix stays)

land pi.display.carousel.autoRotateS: 0 as the shipped default in repo config.json (this is the actual freeze fix: auto-rotate off). Atlas applied it live as a bench stopgap; the deploy is the durable path
[DEPLOY NOTE] changing pi.display.carousel.* requires restarting eclipse-states-http (config injected + cached at its startup) -- fold a states-http bounce into the deploy for carousel-config changes
US-524 cma=256M stays as shipped (benign headroom, no revert -- Atlas)
verification greps the running chromium cmdline: --disable-gpu GONE, --password-store=basic present; autoRotateS effective 0; ruff/lint clean

validationCriteria.action: after deploy + states-http restart, pgrep -a chromium + read the injected DISPLAY_CAROUSEL
validationCriteria.outcome: chromium no longer carries --disable-gpu but keeps --password-store=basic; autoRotateS=0 (carousel does not auto-advance); no freeze

conditionalOutcomes: with GPU back on + auto-rotate off-by-default, the freeze is prevented by auto-rotate being off -- so US-537 (animation-gating) is the safety mechanism for when the F-126 toggle turns it back on
stories.goal: As the operator, I want the durable freeze fix to be auto-rotate-off (GPU left on), matching the CIO's disposition-B decision, so we are not shipping a GPU workaround on trusted hardware.

stories.title: Animation-gating (Atlas RCA #3) -- toggle-safety prerequisite for auto-rotate
acceptance: [Atlas RCA #3 -- now a toggle-safety PREREQUISITE for F-126 auto-rotate] gate the two always-on infinite CSS animations (dashboard.css ribbon-pulse, stop-alarm-pulse) to run ONLY when the ribbon/alarm is actually active; drop unneeded will-change: transform on the carousel track. Reduces the sustained compositing pressure that, combined with auto-rotate, exhausted the GPU command buffer
with GPU on (disposition B) + this gating, auto-rotate ON must NOT reproduce the freeze under sustained carousel navigation (this is what makes the F-126 auto-rotate toggle safe to turn on)
acceptance: with auto-rotate ON, journalctl -u eclipse-dashboard grep -c AllocateRingBuffer stays ~0 + chromium CPU low over a multi-minute session; ruff/lint clean

validationCriteria.action: with animation-gating landed + GPU on, turn auto-rotate ON and sustain carousel navigation for several minutes
validationCriteria.outcome: AllocateRingBuffer count stays ~0, chromium CPU low, no freeze -- the auto-rotate toggle is safe

conditionalOutcomes: gates the F-126 auto-rotate toggle: US-533's auto-rotate toggle is only fully safe once this lands. If it slips, the toggle ships default-OFF with a known caveat.
stories.goal: As the operator, I want turning auto-rotate back on to be safe, so re-enabling it via the F-126 settings toggle cannot re-arm the GPU freeze.
